Subject: Inference qualification: recommended model slate + latency proof pack

Hi Evan / Sara — great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and a recommended next-step plan so we have alignment going into pilot scoping. Attaching a short proof pack with Redwood-verified performance profiles and a prompt set we used during the evaluation.

Key notes from the call:
- Quantify Labs target: 200 concurrent inference TPS at ~512 token requests (customer-ticket summarization, median payload ~420 tokens).
- Primary non-functional asks: p99 latency target < 400ms, predictable cost under sustained load, and regression guards for hallucination on extraction prompts.

Recommended model slate (opinionated):
1) redwood-7b-q -- cost-efficient starter; good for higher TPS with quantization.
2) redwood-13b-ml -- balanced latency/quality for longer context.
3) redwood-70b-s -- highest quality for critical extracts / fallback in canary.

What we attached/linked:
- redwood-performance-profiles-2028.pdf (attachment): per-model TPS and latency percentiles at 256/512/1024 tokens.
- quantify-prompt-pack-v1.zip (attachment): the prompt set we ran during the demo + eval checklist.
- Drive perf folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bRedwoodProofsExample
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/52345/QNTFY-5832

Suggested next steps (short):
- Confirm pilot scope (3-week pilot with 2 models: baseline + fallback).
- We (Redwood) provide a perf snapshot for the exact prompt set and expected traffic shape by EOD tomorrow.
- Procurement to circulate any contract constraints (data residency, retention).

If you want, we can schedule a short 30-min SRE/architecture sync to review request routing, fallback policies, and KV caching assumptions.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Karthik and Markus to prepare the perf snapshots and a pilot estimate.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0122

Quick update — ran the prompt-pack against our perf harness and pulled Redwood-verified snapshots. High-level numbers (512 token window, steady 200 TPS shape, KV cache warm where applicable):

redwood-7b-q
- p50: ~58 ms
- p90: ~135 ms
- p99: ~360 ms
- sustained throughput: ~900 TPS per 8x A10s (batching tuned, continuous batching enabled)

redwood-13b-ml
- p50: ~120 ms
- p90: ~260 ms
- p99: ~520 ms
- sustained throughput: ~220 TPS per 8x A10s (recommended for latency-sensitive fallback)

Notes and recommendations:
- Given Quantify's 200 TPS target, the pragmatic pilot is 7b-q as primary with 13b-ml as canary/fallback. That keeps p99 near your 400ms target in most steady-state cases; p99 may spike on cold cache or pathological prompts — we should include prefix caching for common templates.
- Hosted vs Dedicated cost delta (very rough pilot estimate, 30-day run): Hosted: $X per 1M tokens (est. lower infra ops but higher per-token unit). Dedicated reserved capacity: ~0.6-0.75x per-token infra cost but with commitment. I'll hand this to Markus for a formal quote.
- Attached: link to the perf snapshots & raw traces: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/quantifylabs/QNTFY-5832 and the Drive folder with CSVs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bRedwoodProofsExample
- Prompt-pack used is attached to Naomi's original mail; we'll push a trimmed prompt list to the Drive with labeled failure cases for regression monitoring.

Next steps I can own:
- Produce the latency table CSV and pilot capacity plan by EOD today.
- Produce an initial Hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison (rough) for Markus to formalize into a quote.

If this looks good, Naomi — want me to propose times for an SRE sync with Evan and their infra lead?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
